items.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022
items.q: Sonny I saw grow through his work with Cecil, you could see it, see his improvement.

ctx.x: Did you hear him with various sidemen and if so did you observe anything watching the sidemen that reflected the challenge of playing with Cecil Taylor?

Yeah, not everybody could do it, and not just sideman also like co-partners. I mean you know if you listen to the Mary Lou Williams/Cecil Taylor record they’re not always in accord. Or the Max Roach one, where they — certainly they had no trouble finding a common rhythm but the question of whose voice would be on top was an issue. But there is great music on both of those recordings. There are points at which they’d come together brilliantly. But as for the sidemen he basically developed musicians. Sonny Murray…
You sound like you were or are a musician.
